message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties. Below is a concise but comprehensive overview:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | Natural abundance | ¹H ≈ 99.98 %, ²H ≈ 0.02 % |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an extra electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~53 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| | Density (gas at STP) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar mass | 1.00794 g mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Triple point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Critical point | –82.5 °C (190 K) |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (in H₂ gas at 300 K) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (at 589 nm, 20 °C) |
| | Magnetic susceptibility | –2.8 × 10⁻⁶ cm³ mol⁻¹ (diamagnetic) |
| **Molecular Properties** | Molecular formula | H₂ (most common) |
| | Bond length | 0.741 Å |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Rotational constant | 44.594 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer series (UV/visible) |
| | Color | Colorless (transparent) |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very low (except in supercritical CO₂) |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits: 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH° = –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Oxidation state | +1 (as H⁺) or –1 (as H⁻) |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Acts as a hydride donor (H⁻) in organometallic chemistry |
| | Redox potential | Standard reduction potential of H⁺/H₂ = 0 V (by definition) |
| | pKa of H₃O⁺ | –1.7 (very strong acid) |
| | pKb of H₂O | 15.7 (moderate base) |
| | Solvation energy | ~–0.5 eV per H atom in water |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (for ¹H) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) frequency | 42.577 MHz/T (proton NMR) |
| | Half‑life of tritium | 12.32 years |
| | Decay mode of tritium | β⁻ decay to ³He (β⁻, Q = 18.6 keV) |
| | Binding energy per nucleon | 1.112 MeV (for ¹H) |
| | Nuclear charge radius | 0.877 fm (for ¹H) |
| **Physical State & Phase Behavior** | State at room temperature | Gas |
| | Phase diagram | Exhibits a triple point at 14 K, critical point at 190 K |
| | Vapor pressure | 1 atm at 121 K |
| | Surface tension | 0.002 N m⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Viscosity | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa s (at 300 K) |
| | Compressibility factor (Z) | ~1 (ideal gas behavior) |
| | Specific heat ratio (γ) | 1.41 (monatomic ideal gas) |
| **Optical & Spectroscopic Features** | Lyman series limit | 91.2 nm |
| | Balmer series limit | 364.6 nm |
| | Infrared absorption | 0.0 cm⁻¹ (no permanent dipole, but vibrational transitions in IR are weak) |
| | Raman scattering | Strong due to vibrational modes |
| | UV–Vis absorption | None (transparent) |
| | Photoluminescence | None (non-luminescent) |
| | Fluorescence quantum yield | 0 |
| **Industrial & Technological Uses** | Fuel cell reactant | H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (electrochemical) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ |
| | Metallurgy | Reducing agent for metal oxides |
| | Chemical synthesis | Hydride source (NaBH₄, LiAlH₄) |
| | Cryogenics | Cooling medium (liquid H₂) |
| | Medical imaging | ¹H NMR (MRI) |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen storage (compressed, liquefied, metal hydrides) |
| | Environmental monitoring | Trace detection via mass spectrometry |
| | Space exploration | Fuel for ion thrusters (H₂ + O₂) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Explosion limits in air | Lower: 4 %, Upper: 75 % (v/v) |
| | Flash point | –181 °C (no flash point; ignites at very low temperatures) |
| | Autoignition temperature | 500 °C (in air) |
| | Health hazards | Inhalation of high concentrations can cause hypoxia; cryogenic burns from liquid H₂ |
| | Environmental impact | Greenhouse gas (CO₂) when combusted; negligible in atmosphere otherwise |
| | Storage pressure (compressed gas) | Up to 700 bar (typical industrial) |
| | Storage temperature (liquid) | –253 °C (boiling point) |
| | Storage volume (compressed) | 1 kg H₂ ≈ 70 L at 200 bar |
| | Storage volume (liquid) | 1 kg H₂ ≈ 0.07 L (density ≈ 70 kg m⁻³) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Atomic simplicity**: One proton, one electron, no neutrons (protium).  
- **Highly reactive**: Forms hydrides with metals, acids with nonmetals, and fuels with oxygen.  
- **Low density**: The lightest gas, making it useful for buoyancy and cryogenic applications.  
- **Energy‑rich**: Combustion releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹; fuel cells convert it to electricity with high efficiency.  
- **Isotopic diversity**: Deuterium and tritium are key in nuclear fusion research and isotope labeling.  
- **Spectroscopic importance**: Proton NMR is the backbone of modern medical imaging (MRI).  

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any specific property (e.g., quantum mechanical details, phase diagrams, or industrial processes)!
